# Search reach for IPAS and other residential centres — implementation plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** The brochure site speaks to every kind of residential centre that keeps a 24-hour register or a visitor book, in the words their managers search — with a sector-neutral front door and no claim of a customer it does not have.

**Architecture:** Five new audience pages generated by `tools/build-site.py` (same `page()`/`phead()`/`sec()`/`faq_html()`/`nextlinks()` helpers as the three existing `/for/` pages); the IPAS page rewritten in place; `site/index.html` (hand-written) gets neutral title/description/schema and a card per page; `tools/check-site.py` gains two guards (unique title+description; no customer-claim phrases). The sitemap is hand-maintained.

**Tech Stack:** Python 3 generator committed alongside its output; static HTML under `site/` served by Render with no build step; `tools/check-site.py` run by `check.sh`.

Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-15-site-seo-audiences-design.md` — read its "Voice and truth rules" before writing a word of copy.

## Global Constraints

- **No JavaScript and no `style=""` attributes** on the site (CSP: `default-src 'none'`, `style-src 'self'`). Everything interactive is `<details>`; every rule lives in `site/site.css`.
- **Generated pages are committed.** After editing `tools/build-site.py`: `python3 tools/build-site.py && python3 tools/check-site.py` — both must be clean, and the regenerated files under `site/` are committed with the generator. `check-site.py` also re-runs the generator and fails if any committed page differs.
- **`site/index.html` is hand-written** — edit it directly; the generator never touches it. Its analytics beacon `<script>` must stay byte-identical to the generated pages' (check-site enforces).
- **Every FAQ question in `FAQPage` JSON-LD must appear verbatim in the visible page** — `faq_html(faqs)` and `page(..., faqs)` take the same list, so pass the same list.
- **Truth rules (from the spec):** "built for / designed for / suited to"; never "used by", "trusted by", "our customers", "customers include", "already use", "centres use". No centre is named or located anywhere. The one true claim — built with an accommodation centre manager's feedback — appears only on the IPAS page. Each sensitive-sector page says what the product is **not**.
- **Quiet front door:** `site/index.html` title, description, OG and schema never contain "IPAS" or "direct provision". Those words live on the audience pages.
- **Product fact sheet — write nothing the product does not do.** It does: one daily welfare check-in per resident, closed at local midnight, misses recorded automatically; an In & out door log with a live on-site count; visitors, contractors, suppliers and staff signed in/out with a kind, a name and an optional company; a site staff list for one-tap staff sign-in; roll call / drill / evacuation on every warden's phone, offline, merged afterwards; an evacuation-need code per resident; buildings, floors, rooms, beds and contracted beds, room status (open / under maintenance) with a note, vacancies report; households (families grouped, children marked); authorised absences with return dates, IPAS permitted-absence periods as a warning; house-rules counts (consecutive nights, days-in-window) beside the site's own figures, breach notices recorded; TRC / IRP recorded as printed, never listed; a resident reference of the app's own; append-only records, every record carries who and when; every opening of a resident record logged; Excel downloads and a printable inspection pack; the Sunday Weekly register update email (counts and a link only) and a nightly overnight safeguarding alert (a count of children away overnight with no authorised absence); a nightly House Rules reminder email; unsubscribe links on all three; offline queueing on phones; installable to a tablet home screen; email login codes for supervisors/admins; home-country login check; EU hosting in Frankfurt, one database schema per site, encrypted in transit and at rest; erasure on request and scheduled retention; CSV import with a verdict per line; free trial with sample residents. It does **not**: care plans, medication or nursing records, incident/accident reporting beyond breach notices, rostering, payments, CCTV, ID scanning, badge printing, QR codes, biometric anything, resident-facing app, SMS.
- Copy voice: match the existing `/for/` pages — short declarative sentences, concrete nouns, no marketing adjectives, Irish spelling, em-dashes, no exclamation marks. Read `/for/homeless-hostels/` in `tools/build-site.py` as the model before writing.
- Commit after every task with the attribution footer:
  ```
  Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
  Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01FofqrXrLKdxybZvZYupwRB
  ```

### Task 1: The two guards in `tools/check-site.py`

**Files:**
- Modify: `tools/check-site.py` (inside `check_page()` collect title/description; after the page loop, assert uniqueness; add the phrase scan)

**Interfaces:**
- Produces: `check-site.py` exits non-zero with `problem(...)` lines for a duplicated `<title>` or `<meta name="description">` across pages, and for any of the forbidden phrases (case-insensitive) in any `site/**/*.html`.

- [ ] **Step 1: Prove the guards are missing**

Temporarily append `<p>Trusted by three centres.</p>` to `site/for/student-residences/index.html` and run `python3 tools/check-site.py`. Expected today: it reports only the "differs from what tools/build-site.py produces" problem (because you edited a generated page) — nothing about the phrase. Revert with `git checkout site/for/student-residences/index.html`.

- [ ] **Step 2: Add the guards**

In `check_page(path)`, after the `<title>` check, capture and return the title and description:

```python
    title = re.search(r"<title>(.*?)</title>", text, re.S)
    desc = re.search(r'<meta name="description" content="(.*?)"', text, re.S)
    ...
    return path, (title.group(1).strip() if title else None), (desc.group(1).strip() if desc else None)
```

(`check_page` currently returns `path`; find every caller of its return value — `seen = [check_page(p) for p in pages]` — and unpack accordingly: `seen = [t[0] for t in triples]`.)

After the page loop:

```python
    # Two pages with one title or one description compete with each other in
    # search results and tell nobody which to open. Every page says what it is.
    for what, idx in (("title", 1), ("description", 2)):
        by_value = {}
        for t in triples:
            by_value.setdefault(t[idx], []).append(t[0])
        for value, paths in by_value.items():
            if value and len(paths) > 1:
                problem(f"{what} {value!r} is shared by {', '.join(paths)}")

    # The site must not claim customers it does not have. Written as a guard
    # rather than a note because the temptation is permanent and the cost of
    # one false "trusted by" line, in this sector, is a reputation.
    CUSTOMER_CLAIMS = ("used by", "trusted by", "our customers", "customers include", "already use", "centres use")
    for p in pages:
        low = open(p).read().lower()
        for phrase in CUSTOMER_CLAIMS:
            if phrase in low:
                problem(f"{p}: claims a customer the site does not have ({phrase!r})")
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Prove they fire, then that the site is clean**

Repeat Step 1's temporary edit: `check-site.py` must now also print `claims a customer … ('trusted by')`. Revert. Then duplicate a title temporarily by editing the `page(...)` title of `/for/student-residences/` in `build-site.py` to equal the hostels one, run `python3 tools/build-site.py && python3 tools/check-site.py`, see `title … is shared by`, revert with `git checkout tools/build-site.py site/`. Finally run `python3 tools/check-site.py` on the clean tree: exit 0.

- [ ] **Step 4: Commit**

```bash
git add tools/check-site.py
git commit -m "check-site: every page has its own title and description, and none claims a customer"
```

## Self-review

**Spec coverage.** Home page → Task 6. IPAS rewrite → Task 2. Five pages → Tasks 3–5. Footer nav → Task 3. Sitemap → Tasks 3–6. check-site guards → Task 1. Truth rules → Global Constraints + each page's "is not" paragraph. Quiet front door → Task 6 + constraint.

**Placeholder scan.** Every page has its title, description, H1, lede, section headings, pair items and FAQ questions with the answer's substance. Copy is written by the implementer from those, in the house voice, and read by the reviewer against the fact sheet.

**Consistency.** Paths are identical in the footer list (Task 3), the home cards (Task 6), the sitemap and each `page()` call. Footer order == card order.

**Known intermediate state.** Tasks 2–4 leave check-site with one to three expected broken-link problems until the later pages exist; each task states exactly which. Task 5 is the first fully clean run; Task 6 ends clean.
